Pharaoh

Moses

easy.question: What does the phrase “saying” indicate in the verse?

That Moses left the place
That the speech had no content

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the verse?

Moses spoke and the Lord listened
Aaron addressed Moses and then the Lord arrived

Words or commands are about to be given to Moses
Moses had already answered the Lord

They speak to each other at the same time
The Lord is the speaker and Moses is the one addressed

paragraphs.title: The Law of the Burnt Offering and the Continual Fire

easy.question: What remained burning on the altar throughout the night?
answers: The burnt offering
The ashes
The priest’s garments
easy.explanation: The burnt offering remained on the altar’s fire throughout the night, until morning.

easy.question: What were the priest’s garments made of?
answers: Wool
Linen
Leather
easy.explanation: The priest was commanded to wear a linen garment and linen breeches.

easy.question: What was to be done with the fire on the altar?
answers: It was to be extinguished at night
It was to be lit once a week
It was not to be extinguished
easy.explanation: The verse says that the fire on the altar was not to be put out.

medium.question: What was the correct order of the priest’s actions in the morning?
answers: He removed the ashes, changed clothes, and carried them outside the camp
He carried out the ashes and then put on linen garments
He extinguished the fire and then arranged the burnt offering
medium.explanation: First the priest removed the ashes in his linen garments, then changed clothes and carried them outside the camp.

medium.question: In the phrase “the ashes which the fire hath consumed,” what are the ashes?
answers: Anointing oil
The ashes and remains of the burnt offering
The priest’s garments
medium.explanation: The context shows that the ashes were what remained after the fire consumed the burnt offering.

medium.question: Why did the priest put wood on the fire each morning?
answers: To put out the fire gradually
To clean the altar
To maintain the fire and arrange the offerings on it
medium.explanation: The priest burned wood on the fire, then arranged the burnt offering and the fat of the peace offerings on it.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that handling the ashes took place in two stages and in two locations?
answers: They were first placed beside the altar and then carried outside the camp
They were first burned outside the camp and then returned to the altar
The fire was first extinguished and then relit
challenge.explanation: The priest first placed the ashes beside the altar, then changed clothes and carried them to a clean place outside the camp.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “every morning” imply about adding wood?
answers: Wood was added only when it rained
The action was performed again each morning
Wood was added only in the evening
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that adding wood was a regular action performed every morning.

challenge.question: What is the relationship between the fire burning all night and the morning service?
answers: The night fire canceled the morning service
A new fire was started in the morning
The night fire was maintained, and wood was added to it in the morning
challenge.explanation: The fire was not extinguished during the night; in the morning the priest added wood and continued the offerings.

questions.question: Which detail shows that handling the ashes took place in two stages and in two locations?
answers: They were first placed beside the altar and then carried outside the camp
They were first burned outside the camp and then returned to the altar
The fire was first extinguished and then relit
questions.explanation: The priest first placed the ashes beside the altar, then changed clothes and carried them to a clean place outside the camp.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “every morning” imply about adding wood?
answers: Wood was added only when it rained
The action was performed again each morning
Wood was added only in the evening
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that adding wood was a regular action performed every morning.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the fire burning all night and the morning service?
answers: The night fire canceled the morning service
A new fire was started in the morning
The night fire was maintained, and wood was added to it in the morning
questions.explanation: The fire was not extinguished during the night; in the morning the priest added wood and continued the offerings.

paragraphs.title: The Law of the Grain Offering

easy.question: Who offered the grain offering before the Lord?
answers: The sons of Aaron
All the people
The king of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says that the sons of Aaron offered it before the Lord.

easy.question: What was done with the grain offering that remained after the memorial portion was burned?
answers: It was all burned
Aaron and his sons ate it
It was given to the people
easy.explanation: The remainder of the offering was given for Aaron and his sons to eat.

easy.question: Where was the remaining grain offering eaten?
answers: Outside the camp
In the priest’s house
In a holy place, in the court of the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The verse says that it was eaten in a holy place, in the court of the tabernacle.

medium.question: Why was the grain offering eaten unleavened rather than with leaven?
answers: Because it was intended for all the people
Because it was forbidden to bake it with leaven
Because it was eaten only at night
medium.explanation: The verse expressly says, “It shall not be baken with leaven.”

medium.question: In the phrase “for a sweet savour,” what does “sweet savour” mean?
answers: A pleasing aroma
A sharp smell
A hidden scent
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a pleasing or acceptable aroma rising from the offering to the Lord.

medium.question: What order of actions is described in the verses?
answers: Eating the offering, then presenting it, and finally baking it
Baking it with leaven, then dividing it, and finally burning it
Burning a portion of it, and then eating the remainder
medium.explanation: The priest burned a portion as a memorial offering, and Aaron and his sons ate what remained.

challenge.question: Which part of the grain offering was burned on the altar?
answers: Only the salt
Only the dough
The handful of flour, the oil, and all the frankincense
challenge.explanation: The priest took a handful of the flour and oil and burned all the frankincense on the altar.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the statement “All the males among the children of Aaron shall eat of it”?
answers: Eating it was restricted to males among Aaron’s descendants
Anyone from Israel could eat it
Only the person who brought the offering could eat it
challenge.explanation: The statement limits those entitled to eat it to the male descendants of Aaron, the priests.

challenge.question: What does calling the offering “most holy” teach?
answers: It could be eaten anywhere
It was especially holy, like the sin offering and the trespass offering
It belonged equally to all the Israelites
challenge.explanation: The verse groups it with the sin offering and trespass offering and emphasizes its high degree of holiness and special eating rules.

questions.question: Which part of the grain offering was burned on the altar?
answers: Only the salt
Only the dough
The handful of flour, the oil, and all the frankincense
questions.explanation: The priest took a handful of the flour and oil and burned all the frankincense on the altar.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement “All the males among the children of Aaron shall eat of it”?
answers: Eating it was restricted to males among Aaron’s descendants
Anyone from Israel could eat it
Only the person who brought the offering could eat it
questions.explanation: The statement limits those entitled to eat it to the male descendants of Aaron, the priests.

questions.question: What does calling the offering “most holy” teach?
answers: It could be eaten anywhere
It was especially holy, like the sin offering and the trespass offering
It belonged equally to all the Israelites
questions.explanation: The verse groups it with the sin offering and trespass offering and emphasizes its high degree of holiness and special eating rules.

paragraphs.title: The Continual Offering of the Priest

easy.question: Who offered the offering described in these verses?
answers: Aaron and his sons
All the Israelites
Moses alone
easy.explanation: The verse calls it the offering of Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: How was the tenth part of an ephah divided?
answers: Into three parts
Half in the morning and half in the evening
All in the evening
easy.explanation: The verse says, “half of it in the morning, and half thereof at night.”

easy.question: What was the offering made from?
answers: Beef
Barley bread
Fine flour
easy.explanation: The verse describes it as a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour.

medium.question: What does dividing it between morning and evening show?
answers: The offering was made twice a day
The offering was eaten over two days
The priest could choose when to offer it
medium.explanation: Each half was assigned to a different time, so the offering was made in the morning and evening.

medium.question: In the phrase “In a pan it shall be made with oil,” what preparation is described?
answers: It was prepared or cooked with oil in a pan
It was placed without oil
It was divided into ten pieces
medium.explanation: The verse describes preparing the offering with oil in a pan before bringing it to the Lord.

medium.question: Who was to prepare the offering after the death of the high priest?
answers: Any Israelite
Moses
The next anointed priest from his sons
medium.explanation: The verse says that the priest anointed in his stead from among his sons would offer it.

challenge.question: What was unusual about the priest’s offering compared with offerings that could be eaten?
answers: It was wholly burned and not eaten
It was eaten only in the evening
It was given to the poor
challenge.explanation: The verse says that it was to be wholly burned and not eaten.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “a statute for ever”?
answers: The command was temporary
The rule was intended to continue through the generations
The priest could change the order of the offering
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a permanent, continuing requirement rather than a one-time command.

challenge.question: What does “the priest ... anointed in his stead” mean?
answers: The priest served in Moses’ place
The priest offered on behalf of all Israel
A priest from his sons would continue his role
challenge.explanation: “In his stead” indicates succession, and the verse specifies that the successor would be one of his sons.

questions.question: What was unusual about the priest’s offering compared with offerings that could be eaten?
answers: It was wholly burned and not eaten
It was eaten only in the evening
It was given to the poor
questions.explanation: The verse says that it was to be wholly burned and not eaten.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “a statute for ever”?
answers: The command was temporary
The rule was intended to continue through the generations
The priest could change the order of the offering
questions.explanation: The phrase describes a permanent, continuing requirement rather than a one-time command.

questions.question: What does “the priest ... anointed in his stead” mean?
answers: The priest served in Moses’ place
The priest offered on behalf of all Israel
A priest from his sons would continue his role
questions.explanation: “In his stead” indicates succession, and the verse specifies that the successor would be one of his sons.

To be silent
To speak or declare

Moses had to leave the place
Moses was about to offer a sacrifice

medium.question: What order is described in the verse?

The Lord spoke to Moses, and then a message was given
The Israelites spoke to Moses

medium.question: What does “the Lord spake unto Moses” mean?

The Lord went away
The Lord wrote

challenge.question: What important distinction appears in the verse?

The Lord was the source of the message and Moses received it
The Israelites were the source of the message

Because it describes a journey in the wilderness
Because it lists the names of the priests

It introduces a command or instruction from the Lord

Because it lists the names of the priests

paragraphs.title: The Law of the Sin Offering and the Cleansing of Holy Vessels

easy.question: To whom were the laws of the sin offering given?
answers: Aaron and his sons
All the Israelites
The judges of Israel
easy.explanation: The passage begins by telling Moses to speak to Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: Where was the sin offering eaten?
answers: Outside the camp
In the court of the tabernacle
In the priest’s house
easy.explanation: The offering was eaten in a holy place, in the court of the tabernacle.

easy.question: What was done to the earthen vessel in which the sin offering was cooked?
answers: It was merely washed
It was left in the sanctuary
It was broken
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the earthen vessel was to be broken.

medium.question: Who was permitted to eat the sin offering?
answers: The priest who offered it
Anyone from Israel
Only the person who brought the offering
medium.explanation: The passage says that the priest who offered it was to eat it, and that every male among the priests could eat it.

medium.question: What was to be done if the blood of the sin offering splashed onto a garment?
answers: The garment was burned immediately
The garment was washed in a holy place
The garment was set aside
medium.explanation: The verse commands that the garment on which the blood splashed be washed in a holy place.

medium.question: In the phrase “and shall be scoured and rinsed in water,” what does “scoured” mean?
answers: Broken
Burned
Cleaned or scrubbed thoroughly
medium.explanation: Together with “rinsed in water,” the phrase describes thoroughly cleaning the bronze vessel.

challenge.question: What special rule applied to a sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to make atonement in the holy place?
answers: It could not be eaten and had to be burned
All the people could eat it
It had to be returned to the one who brought it
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes this offering from one that could be eaten and says that it must be burned.

challenge.question: What was the difference between the earthen vessel and the bronze vessel used to cook the offering?
answers: The earthen vessel was washed, and the bronze vessel was broken
The earthen vessel was broken, and the bronze vessel was scrubbed and rinsed
Both vessels were burned
challenge.explanation: The passage says that an earthen vessel was to be broken, while a bronze vessel was to be scoured and rinsed with water.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the sin offering being called “most holy” while still being eaten?
answers: It was unrelated to worship
It could be eaten without restrictions
It was extremely holy, so its consumption was restricted to male priests in a holy place
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes its holiness and restricts eating it to male priests in the court of the tabernacle.

questions.question: What special rule applied to a sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to make atonement in the holy place?
answers: It could not be eaten and had to be burned
All the people could eat it
It had to be returned to the one who brought it
questions.explanation: The passage distinguishes this offering from one that could be eaten and says that it must be burned.

questions.question: What was the difference between the earthen vessel and the bronze vessel used to cook the offering?
answers: The earthen vessel was washed, and the bronze vessel was broken
The earthen vessel was broken, and the bronze vessel was scrubbed and rinsed
Both vessels were burned
questions.explanation: The passage says that an earthen vessel was to be broken, while a bronze vessel was to be scoured and rinsed with water.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the sin offering being called “most holy” while still being eaten?
answers: It was unrelated to worship
It could be eaten without restrictions
It was extremely holy, so its consumption was restricted to male priests in a holy place
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes its holiness and restricts eating it to male priests in the court of the tabernacle.
